body.statement: At each reported \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), whenever the pooled frontier at \(\omega\) certifies one strict common sign, determine \(r_\star(\delta)\) from its finite-dimensional common-law optimization. The candidate \(\omega'\) changes only \(\Psi_{\omega'}(x)\): every candidate law remains in the fixed fiber \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\), whose trial-risk, external-margin, priming-sensitivity, common-history, and placebo-stability constraints remain indexed by \(b\), \(q\), \(\delta\), and \(\omega\). If \(r_\star(\delta)<+\infty\), produce an attaining compatible-law pair \((x,\omega')\) at which the strict side first fails. For every \(r<r_\star(\delta)\), produce a dual certificate that all feasible \(x\) and all \(\omega'\) with \(\lVert\omega'-\omega\rVert_1\leq r\) retain that side. If reversal is infeasible for every \(\omega'\), establish \(r_\star(\delta)=+\infty\) with a dual infeasibility certificate.
body.justification: A sign verdict is decision-relevant only together with the smallest reference-policy change that defeats it while holding the trial, exposure margins, and compatible-law restrictions fixed.
body.gap: Tomer and Biccler (2022) establish mixture-driven time variation, but no published result located gives a fixed-fiber common-law policy radius with an attaining witness, certificates below the radius, and an infinity branch.
body.consumer: Policy makers choosing a reference strain portfolio obtain an auditable robustness radius that does not silently reinterpret the observed trial under each counterfactual mixture.
